description_en: This temple is located to the south of old Patan at Thasikhela Ṭola and has three tiers. Thejhĩgaṭītiles covering the roof of the temple were replaced by copper sheets in 1997. The temple's uppermost roof is gilded and surmounted by a pinnacle. An aniconic stone enshrined in the sanctum is worshipped as Mahālakṣmī and is framed by a metaltoraṇa. Another aniconic stone (also housed in this temple) is worshipped as Viśvakarmā. The temple did not suffer any damages during the earthquakes of 1934 and 2015.No documented evidence has so far been located which can inform us the date of the initial construction of the temple. TheBhāṣā Vamśāvalī(part 2, VS 2023, 3) mentions that Lichhavi King Vīradeva established the temple of Thache Mahālakṣmī to the south of the city when the city of Lalitpur was first founded. However, no other historical document records this information or verifies it. One of the inscriptions on the site mentions that King Śrīnivāsa Malla erected a pillar and offered a golden lion to Mahālakṣmī Mandira in NS 791 (1671 CE). Nevertheless, it is evident that the temple had not yet been constructed by that date; a shrine of the deity must have been there at that time instead. Although theDevamālā Vaṃśāvalī(2013, 76-77) records that King Siddhinarasiṃha Malla commissioned the construction of this temple in NS 750-751, this is not supported by archaeological evidence.An inscription attached to the temple’s wall mentions that Mahālakṣmī Mandira was commissioned by Vīranārāyaṇa Siṃha in NS 821 (1701 CE), a trader (vaiśya) by profession. Furthermore, the inscription (dated NS 850) mentions that King Viṣṇu Malla endowed land to sponsor a fire ritual (śirāhūti yajna). It also mentions that he organised regular worship of Mahālakṣmī on the full moon day of Jyeṣṭha, which is followed by a feast held for seven Brahmins, five Jośīs and four Ācāryas. Over the years, numerous donors offered various objects and ritual materials to the temple.At present, a Rājopādhyāya Brahmin performs the daily ritual worship for Mahālakṣmī. The members of the Dyolā (Poḍe) caste take care of the temple and collect leftover offerings. A procession carries a silver statue of Mahālakṣmī around in a cot every year on the 8thday of the bright fortnight of Caitra (Caite Daśaĩ). Since this temple is the final destination of Dīpaṅkhā Yātrā, the devotees are supposed to leave the rest of the offering materials they have brought with them here. Thekhaḍgajātrā(a procession of displaying a sword of the goddess,thasimalḥ pāyāḥ) starts form this temple on the day of Mahānavamī (9thday of the bright fortnight of Āśvina). There is a tradition that couples get married in this temple premise with the goddess Mahālakṣmī as the witness.
description_ne: ललितपुर शहरको स्थापना गर्दा शहरको सुरक्षार्थ विभिन्न स्थानमा मातृकाका पीठहरू स्थापना गरिएका थिए ।ती मातृकामध्ये ललितपुरको दक्षिणतिर महालक्ष्मीको स्थापना गरिएको थियो । ललितपुरको टुँडिखेल मानिने थसिखेल टोलमा महालक्ष्मीको तीन तह छाना भएको मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको छ । पूर्वाभिमुख यस मन्दिरमा पहिले झिँगटीको छाना थियो, विसं २०५४ सालमा तामाको पाता हालिएको हो । सबैभन्दा माथिल्लो तामाको छानामा सुनको मोलम्बा पनि लगाइएको छ, छानामाथि सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको गजूर छ । मन्दिरको भुइँतलामा रहेको गर्भगृहमा महालक्ष्मी भनेर पूजा गरिने आकृतिविहीन ढुंगा छ, कुनै मूर्ति छैन। सो ढुंगामाथि अष्टमातृका अंकित धातुको तोरण राखिएको छ । महालक्ष्मी सँगै अर्को आकृतिविहीन ढुंगा पनि छ जसलाई विश्वकर्माको मानी पूजा गरिन्छ । विसं १९९० र विसं २०७२ को भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा कुनै क्षति पुगेको थिएन ।यो पीठको स्थापनाको बारेमा स्पष्ट पार्ने कुनै प्रमाण फेला परेको छैन ।Bhāṣā Vamśāvalī(part 2, 2023, 3) मा लिच्छविकालका राजा वीरदेवले ललितपुरको स्थापना गर्दा ललितपुरका विभिन्न दिशामा मातृकाहरू स्थापना गर्ने क्रममा ललितपुरको दक्षिणमा थछे महालक्ष्मी स्थापना गरेको कुरा उल्लेख गरिएको छ । नेपालको इतिहासमा राजा वीरदेवको शासनकालको कुनै प्रमाण हालसम्म नपाइनाले वंशावलीको यो कथनमा पूर्ण रूपले विश्वास गर्न सकिँदैन । पहिले यहाँ कुनै मन्दिर थिएन, खुल्ला ठाउँमा पीठ देवताको रूपमा एउटा शिला मात्र स्थापना गरिएको थियो । मध्यकालमा आएर मात्र महालक्ष्मीको लागि मन्दिर बनाइएको हो । मन्दिर बन्नुभन्दा अघि नै नेसं ७९१ मा राजा श्रीनिवास मल्लले महालक्ष्मी पीठमा खम्बा खडा गरी सुनको सिंह बनाई चढाएका थिए ।Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī(2013,76-77) मा नेसं ७५०-७५१ मा राजा सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लले तीन तलाको मन्दिर बनाएको कुरा लेखिएको छ । वंशावलीको यस कुरालाई अभिलेखीय प्रमाणले खण्डन गरेको छ । मन्दिरमा टाँसिएको शिलापत्रमा नेसं ८२१ मा वैश्य वीरनारायण सिंहले यो मन्दिर बनाएको कुरा लेखिएको छ । नेसं ८५० मा राजा विष्णु मल्लले महालक्ष्मीलाई शिराहूति यज्ञ अर्पण गर्नको लागि जग्गा दान दिएका थिए । जग्गाको आयस्ताबाट प्रत्येक वर्ष ज्येष्ठ शुक्ल पूर्णिमाको दिनमा महालक्ष्मीको पूजा गरी सातजना ब्राह्मण, पाँचजना जोशी र चारजना आचार्यलाई दक्षिणा सहित भोजन गराउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । पछि विभिन्न दाताहरूले मन्दिरमा कृति थप्दै लगेपछि मन्दिर आजको अवस्थामा आइपुगेको हो ।अहिले यस मन्दिरमा राजोपाध्याय ब्राह्मणले नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । मन्दिरको हेरचाह गर्न र भक्तजनहरूले चढाएको भेटी थाप्न द्योला (पोडे) हरू बस्छन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र शुक्ल ८ (चैते दशैं) को दिनमा महालक्ष्मीको चाँदीको मूर्तिलाई खटमा राखेर जात्रा गरिन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष माघ शुक्ल पञ्चमी (श्रीपञ्चमी) र ज्येष्ठ शुक्ल पूर्णिमाको दिनमा गर्नुपर्ने शिराहुति यज्ञ गर्ने परम्परा रोकिइसकेको छ । दीपंखा यात्राको अन्तिम गन्तव्य यही महालक्ष्मी मन्दिर हो । यो अन्तिम गन्तव्य हुनाले यात्रामा सहभागी हुने यात्रुहरूले भेटी चढाउन ल्याएको सामग्री बाँकी भए घर नलगी सबै यहीँ चढाएर जानुपर्ने नियम छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष दशैँको महानवमी (आश्विन शुक्ल नवमी) को दिनमा यस मन्दिरबाट खड्गजात्रा (थसिमल: पाया:) चलाइन्छ । बिहेको मौसममा यस मन्दिरमा आएर महालक्ष्मीलाई साक्षी राखेर विवाह गर्नेहरू थुप्रै हुन्छन् । केही वर्ष पहिलादेखि मन्दिरको प्रचार बढेकोले र मन्दिरको वरपरको क्षेत्रपिकनिकस्पटका रूपमा विकास भएकाले मन्दिरमा आउनेको संख्या बढ्दै गएको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Two stone lions were offered to the temple. Their donors cannot be identified from the inscription.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a stone pillar with a golden lion
historical_events.event_description: King Srīnivāsa Malla erected a pillar with a golden statue of a lion atop it. This pillar is no longer in the temple complex.
Someone called Bhīmabahādura donated a metal flag in VS 1987 (1930 CE). His grandson Kājiratna and grand grandson Suvarṇa Tāmrākāra repaired it.
The legible portion of the inscription mentions that a group of artisans from Jombāhāḥ offered something to Mahālakṣmī.
Govindamāna Śreṣṭha from Bholākhela Bālakumārī plastered the plinth around the temple.

In Nepal, many people believe that when there is a big problem in the country, tears leak from the eyes of gods or sweat comes out of their bodies. When tears flowed from the eyes of Rāto Matsyendranātha in Taḥ Bāhāḥ (LAL0050), thePañcarakṣātext was recited for eight days and a special worship followed by sacrifices was performed in this temple, the Vaiṣṇavī temple of Yappā and the Bālakumārī temple of Kvāṭhachẽ. This event took place before the Mahālakṣmī temple was reconstructed in its current style.
Govindamāna Śreṣṭha from Bholākhela Bālakumārī paved the southern street of the temple in stone.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a shrine for Mahālakṣmī
historical_events.event_description: The Mahālakṣmīpīṭhawas located in an open space until this date (NS 821). Vīranārāyaṇa Siṃha, a trader from Mūlacoka, commissioned the construction of the present temple structure and made an offering of a golden pinnacle. Aguṭhīwas also established to perform the anniversary worship in the temple on the day of Śrīpañcamī.
Nāike Niramāna Siṃha and his family erected a stone pillar with a metal lion atop it.
King Viṣṇu Malla endowed land to sponsor theśirāhūtiyajña(a kind of fire ritual) and made arrangements for a regular worship of Mahālakṣmī to take place on the full moon day of every Jyeṣṭha.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of flags to the main deity
historical_events.event_description: Bhīmabāhādura Tamoṭa from Naḥ Bāhāḥ offered two metal flags.
Govindamana Śreṣṭha of Bholākhela Bālakumārī repaired and plastered the south-west side of the temple.

Nhurche (an artisan from Jombāhāḥ by profession) and his family offered two stone statues of goddesses riding on lions (Simbāhā) in front of Mahālakṣmī. The anniversary worship of these statues takes place every year on the full-moon day of Āśvina.

historical_events.event_name: Replacing jhiṅgaṭī-tiled roof with copper sheets
historical_events.event_description: Sundaralāla Khaḍgī replaced thejhĩgaṭī-tiles on the roof with copper sheets and gilded the top roof.
Govindamana Śreṣṭha of Bholākhela Bālakumārī repaired the temple plinth and commissioned for it to be clad in marble.
An organisation called Buddhi Vikāsa Maṇḍala constructed an artistic brick gate at the entrance of the the temple.
Sudīparatna Tāmrākara repaired the flags donated by Kājīratna Tamoṭa in VS 1987.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a pair of lions
historical_events.event_description: Someone donated the two stone lions which now flank the entrance of the sanctum. The name of the donor could not be deciphered from the inscription.
An artisan from Jombaha clad thetoraṇain brass. This object is fixed above the Mahālakṣmī statue in the sanctum.
Led by artist Ambaradeva of Sātigla (Saugala) Ṭola, Dhanmurta Singh and five other people renovated the roof of the temple. Apāṭīwas also built to the east of the temple on this occasion.
Mahālakṣmīsthāna Vyavasthāpana Samiti (a committee established for the management of the local area) paved the temple courtyard in stone.
During the reign of King Tribhuvan, Jotīrāja, Sidhīrāja, Lakṣmīvīra and others offered the two brass flags which flank the entrance to the sanctum.

Kṛṣṇa Bahādura, a resident of Cāku Bāhāḥ and son of Bhīma Kṛṣṇa, and his wife Pārvatī offered a bell to Mahālakṣmī. It was repaired by their daughters Lakṣmī Kumārī Śilākāra and Viṣṇukumārī in NS 1097 and NS 1100 (VS 2036).
Cinimāyā and others donated a bell in memory of Candra Jālopi.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a metal stand, cladding the pillar
historical_events.event_description: Govindamana Śreṣṭha of Bholākhela Bālakumārī donated a stand for oil lamp inside the sanctum. He also had the pillar clad in brass and offered a bell garland.
